findings: The concrete network contains only strictly forward edges within the actual m-vertex domain. The median sends all lower vertices into the pivot and sends the pivot to all higher vertices; recursion is on disjoint ordered subintervals.
The finite edge-count recursion gives at most m*d edges without requiring duplicate-freeness across unions. Choosing d=ceil(log_2 m) supplies the depth bound, including empty and singleton domains.

The literal two_legs theorem constructs one intermediate vertex between i and j. Its two legs are existing directed edges or zero-length equality legs, yielding an actual allowed directed walk of length at most two.

The finite-index embedding preserves injectivity and edge count. The constructed PathWitness deliberately exposes the existing four-hop interface, while finEdges_short proves the stronger local two-hop fact.
The disjoint-chain union uses this concrete witness with monotone ambient logarithmic budget; H consists of actual original-reachability candidates and has the stated ambient n*ceil(log_2 n) bound.
scope: Concrete finite two-hop median path networks and a four-hop chain-union interface with logarithmic size. No fast runtime, linear size or iterated-logarithmic supershortcut bound is proved here.
